newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bond traders turned attention to European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) amidst uncertainty over the future of the planned third stage, a single European currency.
"We have seen everything (traded) a little bit," said one bond dealer. "Mainly it is very calm. People are looking at EMU and official statements. We have to wait and see what happens."

On Monday, comments by French finance minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said France needed more time to study the plan, which calls for keeping budget deficits under strict control once the single currency has been introduced.
Uncertainty about EMU should be positive for Swiss bonds, if it drives investors seeking refuge from prospective Euro-storms into the relative safety of the Swiss market.
But the EMU worries also undermined German Bunds, which may have had negative implications for the Swiss market Monday.

Three-month EuroSwiss futures ended down. The short end of the market continued to drop as short-term interest rates edged back up. Rates had declined in recent weeks on hopes the Swiss National Bank would continue to lower interest rates. That now appeared less likely due to the Swiss franc's easier tone.
The Swiss market is also waiting for domestic first quarter gross domestic product (GDP) data expected on Thursday.
Euro Swiss francs down seven at 98.50.
